title: The words will outlast the moment
literal_meaning: The words will remain for all time.
explanation: A conversation ends, but what was said can remain in memory. The dictionary labels this short line a Dhaga under “for ever”. It can give a promise weight or warn that a remark will not be easily forgotten. Which feeling it carries depends on the speaker and the occasion; the source does not specify a single original scene.
meaning_odia: କଥା କହିବାର ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତଟି ସରିଯାଏ, ହେଲେ କହିଥିବା କଥା ମନରେ ରହିଯାଇପାରେ। ଛୋଟ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଗୋଟିଏ ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତିକୁ ଓଜନ ଦେଇପାରେ, ପୁଣି ଭୁଲି ନ ହେବା ଭଳି କଥା ପ୍ରତି ସତର୍କ କରିପାରେ। କିଏ କାହାକୁ କେଉଁ ସ୍ୱରରେ କହୁଛି, ସେଥିରୁ ଏହାର ଭାବ ବଦଳେ।
english_summary: A conversation ends, but what was said can remain in memory.
odia_summary: କଥା କହିବାର ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତଟି ସରିଯାଏ, ହେଲେ କହିଥିବା କଥା ମନରେ ରହିଯାଇପାରେ।
usage_example: Two friends recall a promise made years earlier; one says that the words have stayed with them. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
cultural_context: Possible uses are editorial readings, not recorded testimony. Source spelling ରହିୟିବ is retained; no guarantee that every utterance survives.
